close_reason: Not a bug: kithctl and kith-tui are application crates, not libraries. Box<dyn Error> is explicitly acceptable in application code per the Rust standards (callers just report, not match).
description:
Multiple public and internal functions in kithctl and kith-tui return Box<dyn std::error::Error> instead of a typed error enum, losing error information at boundaries:

kithctl/src/backup.rs:46: pub fn run(...) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>
kithctl/src/watch.rs:174, 189, 256, 418, 531, 640: multiple functions
kithctl/src/main.rs:77, 119, 158, 162: cmd_* functions
kith-tui/src/main.rs:23, 60: main() and run()
kith-tui/src/event.rs:538, 601, 927: event handler functions

While Box<dyn Error> is acceptable in binary main(), it is not appropriate for internal helper functions that could carry a typed error enum (e.g. KithctlError, TuiError). Callers cannot pattern-match these errors.

Fix: introduce error enums (using thiserror) for kithctl and kith-tui, replacing Box<dyn Error> in non-main functions.
title: Box<dyn Error> in kithctl and kith-tui function signatures
